The test image shows a tomato leaf with:
- Widespread brownish-gray necrosis covering most of the leaf
- Fuzzy/velvety texture on the necrotic areas (characteristic sporulation)
- Yellow-green areas still present at margins
- Soft, spreading decay pattern with no distinct concentric rings or defined lesion spots

The grayish-brown fuzzy sporulation strongly suggests **Gray Mold** (Botrytis cinerea). Let me confirm with one reference image.

The reference shows Gray Mold (Botrytis) on fruit, but the pathogen's hallmark gray fuzzy sporulation is visible. My test image shows a leaf with the same grayish-brown fuzzy/velvety necrotic tissue — the large-scale soft decay with grayish sporulation is consistent with Botrytis cinerea affecting leaf tissue.

No other class fits as well:
- Early Blight: concentric rings pattern (not present)
- Late Blight: dark water-soaked lesions, white downy growth on underside
- Septoria: small circular spots with white centers
- Leaf Mold: yellow patches on upper surface, olive-green spores below

The widespread grayish-brown soft necrosis with fuzzy sporulation texture matches **Gray_Mold**.
